value.rationale: The first separation of a global minimum-feedback ranking rule and a stationary random-walk rule is a natural structural boundary already highlighted by the disparity-index literature. The complete threshold layer shows that the first disagreement is rigid rather than arbitrary: every Markov set is a singleton strictly contained in the Slater set, and only two asymmetric tournament types occur. This supplies a concrete structural explanation for the known one-order gap between disparity and separation.
